text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government change expected next week and Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti just one of the candidates to head reshuffled cabinet.
- In his first visit to Gaza, Crown Prince Hassan delivers a message from King Hussein to PLO leader Yasser Arafat; holds comprehensive talks with Palestinian leader over the preservation of peace.
- Islamic Action Front (IAF) party forms a defence counsel for Jordanian soldier who shot Israeli schoolgirls.
- Crown Prince Hassan says in Gaza "Jordan rejects settlements and the distortion of the status quo in Jerusalem."
- King Hussein's visit to Israel saved the peace process, emphasis on the rejection of violence and continuing peace talks.
- Landslide victory for Islamists in Jordan University election.
- The palace's initiative succeeded in resuming the Palestinian track; Arafat praises the efforts of King Hussein in pushing the peace process ahead.
- Opposition parties condemn the killing of children and call for a fair trial for the gunman soldier.
- Talks between a visiting Saudi business delegation and Jordanian business leaders tackle investment opportunities.
- Two hurt in a shootout in Maan over personal disputes.
- King's personal warmth makes him Israel's favourite Arab leader.
